During mining operations, the overall impact on the surface-water resources will be related to the extent of development in Tracts II and III. As development progresses, each tributary drainage basin affected will be isolated from the overall drainage systems of Sarpy and Tullock Creeks by temporary detention structures. Isolation of tributary drainage may result in the depletion of surface-water runoff by as much as fifty percent of that normally expected from the affected drainage. Water losses will result from evaporation from pond surfaces, consumptive use, and infiltration to the ground water table.
Under natural conditions runoff from the upper reaches of the tributaries seldom travels all the way to the main streams unless it is in response to a high-intensity runoff event. Most of the runoff normally infiltrates into the alluvium/colluvium of the tributary stream before it reaches the main stream, hence, little of this water contributes to stream flow. Therefore, the impact of the detention ponds would be to prevent only the runoff from flood events from running directly to the main stream. This water, however, will be released to the tributary stream when the quality of the water meets applicable water quality standards.
The overall reduction in streamflow of Tullock, East Fork Sarpy, and Sarpy Creeks as results of the mining operation is expected to be minimal.
